notes.title: YARG is now more affordable!
notes.notes:
Hello, everyone! Hope you've all had an amazing New Year's!

I'm here with a quick update to let all y'all know that YARG is now [b]$3.99[/b] (formerly [i]$5.99[/i])! That's like a 33% discount, except permanent!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/9ae80d72536ef7947f8b4c636eec23205b55b7d2.png[/img]

There isn't any particular reason for why I've decided now is the right time to do this. I've always put YARG up for Steam's seasonal sales, which dropped the price regardless, so I figured I might as well go all the way! Also, looking at games of similar genre and scope, I feel like $3.99 is more appropiate for the sort of game YARG is.
Don't forget, this was my first substantial game project, so I'm still learning a lot of this stuff!

A massive thank you to everyone who's supported me on this whole journey! I've [url=https://www.santumerino.com/blog/YARG-postmortem/]written about it at length elsewhere[/url], but I cannot overstate the impact that this project had (and still has) on me and my work. I'm glad I could put this lil' platformer out there for people to play :)

As always, feel free to [url=https://bsky.app/profile/santumerino.com]@ me on [strike]Twitter[/strike] Bluesky[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!

- Santum

notes.title: Steam Awards? Sounds kinda epic...
notes.notes:
Hiya, gang!

I got an e-mail from Steam informing me of this year's upcoming (as of writing) Steam Awards, suggesting I make a quick post to let y'all know about it! So this is that!

YARG came out last year, meaning it's eligible for the Labor [i][sic][/i] of Love award! And lemme tell ya, after all this time, with all the updates and the recently released free prologue?
...I wouldn't have done all that if I hated the game, I tell ya that much.

Now, I'm not crazy, I am well-aware that this tiny indie game is but a drop in the ocean of 2D pixel art platformers. But I have a proposition to make that, I believe, no other game of this genre can compete with...
...wouldn't it be [i]really funny[/i] if YARG got an award? Like, c'mon now. You know it would be hilarious.

And just to sweeten the deal a lil' bit, you'll notice that this whole shebang is taking place during the Autumn Sale. 20% off for what's probably gonna be this year's Labour of Love award winner? Sounds like a great deal to me, I dunno!


...OK, jokes aside, this game holds an extremely special place in my heart. It was my first large-scale project, and I spent years on it. Whether I got 0 sales, 5 sales, or 30 total sales with 4 people returning it, it genuinely doesn't matter. I am still hugely appreciative of everyone who decided to give this game even just a look. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart.

As always, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!

- Santum

notes.title: YARG: Prologue is OUT!
notes.notes:
Wahey! It's YARG's one-year anniversary!

To celebrate, I have taken the old YARG demo (from the 2022 Steam Next Fest), revamped it, gave it a facelift, re-recorded a few voicelines here and there, and turned it into the official [b]YARG: Prologue[/b]!!
If you weren't here back then, be prepared for a FREE stand-alone experience with 7 levels from the full game, new characters, a new story, and perhaps even a cheeky bit of lore™!

Also, depending on when you're reading this, the full game may or may not be on its highest discount yet, at a whole 20% off! If you enjoy the prologue, why not see where the rest of the story goes? :)

I've also written a little bit about my thoughts on this whole journey, which you can find as a [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino/status/1703091293834871114]thread on Twitter[/url]. But TL;DR: I am very happy with how the game's been evolving, and I am so excited for the future. Thank you to everyone who's been here, even if you only found out about the game just now.

Anyhow! Time for some good ol' patchnotes!

[h2]YARG Demo 1.1/YARG: Prologue changes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] The old YARG demo has been turned into an official prologue!
[*] Implemented all the bugfixes and changes from the full game.
[*] Re-recorded some of the ending voicelines, to bring their tone/mood closer to the full game.
[*] Fixed possible softlock involving a door and dying too many times.
[*] Improved the door sprites.
[/list]

As always, if you come across any bugs, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! I'm gonna go celebrate, see ya soon!

- Santum

notes.title: YARG: Update v1.1.1
notes.notes:
Well hello there! I've got a new update for all of y'all!

This one's labelled as if it were a minor update, but it actually contains a bunch of fixes, improvements, and an entirely new feature: [b]Discord Rich Presence![/b] I decided not to go with "v1.2" for this one though, because...
...well, let's just say that I still have more plans for the future of YARG :)

Anyway, let's get into the patchnotes!

[h2]v1.1.1 changes:[/h2]
[h3]Added:[/h3]
[list][*]Discord Rich Presence! Let all your friends know you were stuck for 15 minutes in that one level where all the lasers are aiming at you![list][*]You can enable and disable this in the Options menu. If you already had a save file from an earlier version, it defaults to being disabled. Otherwise, it defaults to being enabled.[/*][/list][/*][/list][list][*]Every level in the game now has a name! These are still subject to change, but I’m good with how they currently are.[/*][*]You can now skip the every cutscene except the ending ones by pressing P (you could already do this with the splash screen).[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixed:[/h3]
[list][*]When you move your spawn point in Assist Mode, it first checks whether that position is valid. This check is now more accurate.[/*][*]The particle effect when a sawblade collides with a surface has been restored.[/*][*]You can now pause while playing a custom level.[/*][/list]
[h3]Changed:[/h3]
[list][*]Changed the sawblade’s hitbox to make it more forgiving.[/*][*]Improved one of the backgrounds.[/*][*]Switched my Fusion 2.5 license to the “Developer” tier, meaning I no longer need to prominently feature Clickteam logos in my game.[/*][/list]

As always, if you come across any bugs, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!

- Santum

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/c798b2db6abbbc2c45cd4ae92585ec4d4e389ac2.png[/img]

...by the way, did you guys play the YARG demo? It used to be available back before the full game was released, but I delisted it once the game came out. It was like a prequel to the main story, with its own characters, cutscenes, voice acting, mechanics, etc.

If you didn't get the chance to do it, then... stay tuned!

notes.title: YARG: Update v1.1
notes.notes:
Hello hello hello! Hope everyone's had an excellent New Year!
I've been working on an update to the level editor for a few months (practically since launch lol), and the first half of that is finally ready to share!

So, I'm proud to announce the first content update for YARG: [b]the Level Editor Facelift Update[/b]!!!
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/4c92f9a3a393ccc4ad492df5a8fab29e53ab9ecd.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/4c92f9a3a393ccc4ad492df5a8fab29e53ab9ecd.gif[/img][/url]

The level editor has always been my least favourite bit of the game. It was functional, and I used it to make every level in the game, but there were a few weird oddities and seemingly impossible to solve bugs with it. Also, it didn't work too well on controllers.
This update remedies all that! The UI has been simplified and generally made a lot clearer. There are now sound effects and music. And controller support has been rebuilt from the ground up. Overall, I think this is a lot more fit for a proper finished game!

I'm very happy with this current iteration of the level editor, but there's still a few more things coming to it! My plans for it needed this UI to be released first, and it'll take some time to get all that up and running, so consider this part one of a two-part level editor update series!

[hr][/hr]
Alongside the level editor, I've also managed to throw in a few more minor improvements, ranging from adding some missing sound effects to a new visual effect for a major moment in the game. Here are the patchnotes!

[h2]v1.1 changes:[/h2]
[h3]Added:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Gave the level editor a facelift!
[list]
[*] Cleaner UI! Streamlined controls! A brand-new music track! Wow!!
[/list]
[*] Added a "click" sound effect to buttons that were missing it.

[*] Visual improvement: added some particle effects for the last level.
[/list]
[h3]Removed:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The previous level editor has been removed.
[/list]
[h3]Fixed:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The "Loading..." text that appears when loading a custom level is no longer animated.
[list]
[*] ...not that you would've noticed it was animated in the first place, since the engine freezes the screen when loading a new scene anyway
[/list]
[*] The game's music will now preload on launch. This should hopefully prevent some desync that was happening every so often.

[*] Squashed some bugs here and there.
[/list]

As always, if you come across any bugs, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!
- Santum

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/efe77b73036525a112f33a534d08804f9a814e96.png[/img]

notes.title: YARG: Update v1.0.2c
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!
If you've seen the last patchnote, you know that the game has suffered from a huge problem since the beginning: on some people's computers, the game would refuse to load cutscenes properly (often just playing the audio but not showing the video).
I thought I fixed it last time, but as it turns out the bug was still lurking underneath the surface, ready to anti-climactically ruin the ending for another player...

Today, I say [b]no more![/b]

I have reworked the cutscene system entirely, re-rendered every video, and checked and double-checked everything to no end (although to be fair, cutscenes always worked fine on my PC. That's why this bug is so dastardly)...
Today's the day this bug will meet its [i][b]RUIN!!!![/b][/i]

...ahem. I got a bit carried away there, sorry. Point is, I think I fixed the cutscene bug for real now. Here's the patchnotes!

[h2]v1.0.2c changes:[/h2]
[h3]Fixed:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Replaced Clickteam's own Active Direct Object extension with [url=https://github.com/defisym/OpenFusionExamples]the FFMpeg object by Defysim[/url].
[*] Updated the credits accordingly.
[*]  Re-rendered all cutscenes as MP4.
[/list]

As always, if you come across any bugs, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!
- Santum

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/6c344b8bf18917003bd44eae0aeadc77eba8aff8.png[/img]

notes.title: YARG: Update 1.0.2b
notes.notes:
Hello hello hello! How's everyone doing?
This is a very small update, so small that it doesn't even get its own number. It involves the game's cutscene system.
For some reason, the game will be able to load some cutscenes perfectly fine, and fail to load others. I came across this issue several times during development, and I could've sworn I fixed it, but apparently it could still happen!
I suspect the problem has something to do with the file format of the cutscenes (something about codecs...). This update changes them from AVI to WMV, which I'm hoping will fix the issue. Let me know if it does!

[h2]v1.0.2b changes:[/h2]
[h3]Fixed(?):[/h3]
[list]
[*] Switched all cutscenes from AVI to WMV in the hopes they'll load properly now.
[/list]
[h3]Changed:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Locked cutscenes to 30 FPS to prevent stuttering.
[/list]

As always, if you come across any bugs, feel free to [url=https://twitter.com/santumerino]@ me on Twitter[/url] or send me an email! Thanks!
- Santum

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/80f7f5df10406c2f8e1c4c5f34dc306603c364c7.png[/img]

notes.title: YARG is done!
notes.notes:
Well hello everyone! Long time to talk, eh?

I've been busy with a bunch of stuff, most of it personal (studying and whatnot), and some of it actually relevant to you guys (developing the Freakin Game).

That first part took up most of my time, so after the demo I could only manage to spend a little bit of time on the game. But it all added up, and I am happy to announce that [b]YARG has finished development, and a release date is coming very soon.[/b] [strike](I actually finished it a few weeks ago but shh)[/strike]

The game has over 30 levels, two endings, four animated (to the best of my ability) cutscenes, a level editor and the ability to play other people's custom levels, 85 voice-acted lines of dialogue, and [i]so many[/i] fun little secrets I can't wait for people to discover.

Needless to say, I am absolutely ecstatic and I cannot wait for all of y'all to get your hands on this game! This is my first long-term game project and, to be honest, I can't believe I managed to do as much as I did.

I hope you'll all enjoy it when it comes out soon! Next post will have the release date and a new trailer to accompany it.

See you then!

notes.title: YARG: On Air!
notes.notes:
Well hello there, gamers! Y'all are collectively looking quite handsome today, did you know that?

Anyway, I'm here to let you guys know that you are all cordially invited to a livestream happening on the 21st of February! It'll be a lot of fun, you'll see.
What's the occasion, you ask?

Well, it's just a little something called [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/nextfest]the Steam Next Fest[/url]! And YARG will be there, with a whole entire demo!!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/6b8a3f0dee75c1483507987d2c44f846fbeeeb26.png[/img]

[b][i]PAQ (Possibly Asked Questions):[/i][/b]
[list]
[*][b]What's the demo gonna have, content-wise?[/b]
It'll have 7 levels from the full game, showing a variety of obstacle types. Plus, a whole new story featuring new characters!
[*][b]Wait, why is there a new story?[/b]
I wouldn't be able to fit all of the lore™ into the demo, and only putting some parts of it in would've just been unsatisfying for you [i]and[/i] for me.
Instead (not to spoil too much) there's a bit of a prequel situation going on in here!
[*][b]Will none of the characters from the full game appear in the demo?[/b]
You'll see.
[*][b]That's... oddly cryptic.[/b]
Eheheh...
[*][b]OK, I don't like this. But I [i]do[/i] like what I'm hearing about this demo! What was the date again?[/b]
The demo will be up [u]from February 21 at 10 AM Pacific, to the 28th, for the Steam Next Fest[/u]!
I'll probably bring it back in the future, but for now, if you want to play it, you can do so during that time!
[*][b]What if I miss the livestream?[/b]
First of all, wow. Just... just wow.
Second of all, no worries! It'll be re-run several times a day, for the duration of the event (except on days I forget).
[/list]

That's it! I cannot wait for people to play the demo, I am genuinely really happy with it. Hope to see you there!

notes.title: YARG's OST (Oh! Super T-epic!)
notes.notes:
Hey gamers!

YARG didn't have a soundtrack for the longest time. I don't know how to do music (believe me, [url=https://youtu.be/UmTgr6963N8]I tried[/url]) and I wasn't really able to reach out to any musicians. So, the game only had SFX and voice lines in terms of audio.

Thankfully, my brother happens to be pretty gosh darn good at making music, and he was kind enough to donate some of his time to making some bangers for the game. The music in YARG is adaptive; as more gameplay elements (lasers, drones, saws, ██████ and the like...) appear in the levels, the music slowly gets built upon.

Here's a little preview! There's more stems n such, but I'm keeping those as surprises :)

[previewyoutube=gHO2a44b-EA;full][/previewyoutube]

I wanted the song to be more on the chill side, because I felt that having a super intense song would just be too much when combined with the intensity of the gameplay. What do you think?

If you want to hear more sick-ass music, and don't mind a bit of Spanish, check out [url=https://open.spotify.com/artist/76ZJ4kYgtsGFr5L7I8dIa9]my brother's Spotify account![/url]

Thank you for reading this post, gamers 😎😎😎

notes.title: The power of level editors
notes.notes:
YARG comes with a level editor. This is actually the same editor [i]I'm[/i] using to make all the levels in the game, so anything that you see in the game, you can do in the editor.

That said, it went through a complete redesign lately to make it look less... prototype-y? I still have to do a bit more work on it but it's already at a point I'm pretty happy with.

[i]Before:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/3e824bfd6d3c6dff1260afba1b322940d8aabe90.png[/img]

[i]After:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41123243/c7193de29d2fdbedab8336f4a7002c2874dc77dd.png[/img]

This is my first time making a level editor, so there were some particularly annoying bugs (such as one where the game refused to load level files correctly) which I've thankfully fixed already. Still, as soon as the game comes out, I'll be keeping an eye out and squashing any other bugs that might pop up.

Without a level editor, I'm not sure I would've gotten this far in the game's development (TL;DR: The engine I'm using for this game treats every level as its own separate mini-game with its own separate code which would've needed to be duplicated and maintained manually every time I changed anything), so I'm hoping it'll be useful, or even just fun, for y'all as well.

See ya later, gamers!

PS: I went through the game and added some more decorative tiles to the levels so they look less plain. I'll update the store screenshots soon 😎
